requirements.text: Posting an object with the Flask test client's json parameter marks the request as JSON, request.get_json() returns the same object, and returning it produces an HTTP 200 application/json response with the same data.
A request body containing the JSON string alpha with content type application/x+json is recognized as JSON and request.get_json() returns alpha.
A malformed body sent with content type application/json causes request.get_json() to produce HTTP 400 instead of executing a successful JSON response.
Calling jsonify with no positional or keyword arguments returns an application/json response whose JSON value is null.
Calling jsonify with multiple positional values returns an application/json array that preserves positional order and values.
Calling jsonify with keyword arguments returns an application/json object; the default provider sorts keys and emits compact output outside debug mode.
The default JSON provider escapes non-ASCII characters when ensure_ascii is true and emits the literal Unicode character when ensure_ascii is false.
Calling jsonify with both positional and keyword arguments raises TypeError with the message app.json.response() takes either args or kwargs, not both.
